Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

Current bug report: {'summary': 'Use of ThreadLocals in ToStringStyle and HashCodeBuilder trigger memory leaks in container environments', 'description': "The thread local in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringStyle is created but never removed and no API is provided to remove it. If a webapp's use of LANG triggers the loading of this class, a reference chain will be created that will cause a memory leak on web application reload.\nSee <http://markmail.org/thread/uetw2fdrsqgbh2cv> for more info.\n"}

Proceed to fault localisation and produce a step-by-step diagnosis.

The failing test `HashCodeBuilderTest.testReflectionObjectCycle()` is attempting to assert that the `getRegistry()` method in `HashCodeBuilder` returns `null`. However, based on the current bug report, there seems to be a memory leak issue related to the usage of ThreadLocals in `ToStringStyle` and `HashCodeBuilder`.

Looking at the implementation of the `getRegistry()` method in `HashCodeBuilder`, it retrieves a `ThreadLocal` value, but there is no mechanism to clear or remove this value. If this `ThreadLocal` value is set in a container environment like a web application, it can lead to memory leaks when the web application is reloaded.

The issue report indicates that the `ThreadLocal` in `ToStringStyle` is created but never removed, and there is no API provided to remove it. This can create a reference chain that leads to a memory leak on web application reload.

To further diagnose the fault, it would be essential to analyze the usage of `ThreadLocals` in `HashCodeBuilder`, `ToStringStyle`, and related classes to determine where the cleanup or removal of `ThreadLocal` values should occur to prevent memory leaks in container environments.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
